cf.title: Preserve replication origin OIDs in pg_upgrade

input.subject: [PATCH] Preserve replication origin OIDs in pg_upgrade

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and a committer who knows the area took part in the design. Three fixable points remain. demand-1: the main benefit depends on a separate pg_commit_ts migration whose status the thread does not give. replication-ondisk-2: upgrades from clusters before 17 are now refused in cases that pass on HEAD. replication-ondisk-1: the check that justifies those refusals can be bypassed while apply workers run. A committer has to decide the pre-17 behaviour change.

brief.title: Preserve subscription OIDs and replication origin IDs in pg_upgrade
brief.problem: Commit timestamp records store the numeric roident, but pg_upgrade lets CreateSubscription() take the lowest free roident in the new cluster, so origins can get new or swapped IDs. If pg_commit_ts were carried over, this would cause spurious update_origin_differs conflicts. Origins not owned by a subscription, such as ones made by external tools, are lost today.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 0001 preserves pg_subscription.oid, so origin names like pg_<suboid> stay the same. Patch 0002 has pg_dumpall dump all replication origins as global objects in binary-upgrade mode and recreates each one with its old roident and, if tracked, its remote_lsn. CreateSubscription() skips origin creation in binary-upgrade mode, and the subscription state checks now run for all old versions.
user_visible_surface: New support function binary_upgrade_create_replication_origin(oid, name, lsn); binary_upgrade_replorigin_advance() is removed.
pg_dumpall --binary-upgrade emits replication origins, also with --globals-only.
pg_upgrade rejects a new cluster that has any replication origins, and checks max_active_replication_origins against tracked origins instead of subscriptions.
pg_upgrade from clusters before 17 now rejects subscriptions with a missing origin or relations not in 'i' or 'r' state.
author_claims: This is a prerequisite for preserving pg_commit_ts across pg_upgrade.
User-created origins are now kept with their IDs and remote_lsn.
For old clusters before 17, enabled subscriptions resume from the migrated remote_lsn, and duplicates are no worse than on HEAD.
Rejecting origin-less subscriptions from old clusters is harmless.
brief.thread_state: Many reviewers, mostly from Fujitsu, reviewed the patch through v22, and Amit Kapila steered the design toward preserving IDs for all source versions. The latest change applies the subscription state checks to clusters before 17; Shveta agreed, and no committer has said the patch is ready.
unclear: The pg_commit_ts migration it serves is a separate patch, and the thread does not say whether that patch is accepted.
There is no test of an upgrade from a cluster before 17 in the patch, only manual runs.
No committer has reviewed the behaviour change for old clusters before 17, which are now rejected in cases that worked before.

prior_attempts.title: Patch for migration of the pg_commit_ts directory
prior_attempts.what_is_different: This proposal does not migrate pg_commit_ts. It preserves the roident values that such a migration needs, and it also keeps origins that are not owned by subscriptions.

objections.title: Main benefit depends on a pg_commit_ts migration not yet accepted
objections.failure_scenario: A committer pushes both patches, but the pg_commit_ts migration does not land in the same release. Upgrades from clusters before 17 that worked before are now rejected for missing origins or relations not in 'i' or 'r' state. The roident preservation that justified this change protects no data in that release.
objections.argument: Messages #1 and #26, and the 0002 commit message, give one motivation: keeping roident stable so a copied pg_commit_ts stays valid. Amit Kapila notes in message #26 that the roident value only matters from PG19 onward. Message #2 says subscription OID preservation was declined before for lack of a strong motivation, and this patch borrows its motivation from a separate patch whose status the thread does not give. The other benefit, keeping origins made by external tools, has no user report in the thread.
objections.author_must_show: Is the pg_commit_ts migration patch agreed for the same release, or which users of external replication tools have reported losing origins in pg_upgrade?

critic.reasoning: The 0002 commit message calls the patch a prerequisite for pg_commit_ts migration, and the thread does not give that patch's status. Amit Kapila's engagement lowers the concern, but the thread shows no user report for the independent gain of keeping user-created origins.

objections.title: New pg_upgrade refusals for pre-17 clusters where filtering would do
objections.failure_scenario: An operator upgrades a PG14 subscriber whose table sync is stuck in 'd' state, or one whose origin was dropped by hand. HEAD upgrades it and restores the subscription disabled. With v22 the check refuses the upgrade, and the operator must fix the old cluster first.
objections.argument: These refusals exist only to keep tablesync origins and origin-less subscriptions from causing trouble after migration (messages #88, #90). For pre-17 sources, pg_subscription_rel is not migrated and subscriptions come back disabled, so origins named pg_<suboid>_<relid> carry no state the new cluster can use. Skipping those origins at dump time would keep the current pre-17 behaviour. Message #90 calls the refusal harmless, but no committer has weighed it, and the patch has no pre-17 upgrade test.
objections.author_must_show: Why reject pre-17 clusters in these states instead of leaving out tablesync origins and recreating a missing subscription origin, as HEAD does today?

critic.reasoning: The v22 commit message confirms that upgrades from clusters before 17 are now refused in cases that pass on HEAD. Amit Kapila's argument in message #26 covered restrictions on the new cluster, and the thread does not discuss skipping tablesync origins at dump time.

objections.title: Tablesync origin leak check is racy for old clusters before 17
objections.failure_scenario: A user upgrades a PG16 subscriber that has a table in 'i' state, which the check accepts. While pg_upgrade runs, the old apply worker launches a tablesync worker, which creates origin pg_<suboid>_<relid> before pg_dumpall reads pg_replication_origin. That origin is migrated, and later DROP SUBSCRIPTION leaves it behind.
objections.argument: Message #85 states that apply workers can run during pg_upgrade when the source is PG16 or older. Message #88 adds the state check because migrated tablesync origins cannot be dropped once pg_subscription_rel is not carried over. The v22 commit message allows relations in 'i' state. A check taken before the dump does not bound what the dump later sees while workers keep running.
objections.author_must_show: For sources before 17, what stops a tablesync origin from being created between check_old_cluster_subscription_state() and pg_dumpall, or would it be safer not to dump pg_<suboid>_<relid> origins from such sources?

critic.reasoning: Message #85 says apply workers can run during pg_upgrade when the source is before 17, and the check accepts relations in 'i' state. The thread does not say what stops a tablesync origin from appearing between the check and the dump.

refuted.title: Main motivation rests on a pg_commit_ts migration that is not yet accepted
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer adds subscription OID preservation, a new binary-upgrade origin function, and new pre-17 upgrade rejections. The pg_commit_ts migration never lands. Users upgrading from PG16 or older are then refused for relations in a non 'i'/'r' state, and the roident guarantee protects no carried-over commit timestamps.
refuted.argument: Message #2 reports that an earlier attempt to preserve subscription OIDs was not accepted for lack of strong motivation. The new motivation is the pg_commit_ts migration (message #1, v22-0002 commit message), and [P11], an entry for that migration, was withdrawn with no recorded reason. The doc hunk still says commit timestamps are not preserved. Keeping user-created origins is a separate benefit, but message #1 and the commit message present it as secondary.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the pg_commit_ts migration patch active and agreed in principle, and if it never lands, does keeping user-created origins justify the new pre-17 upgrade rejections by itself?

precedents.title: Patch for migration of the pg_commit_ts directory

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1, which states the dependency on the pg_commit_ts migration without a precedent. [P11] records no reason for its withdrawal, so it cannot support the point.

refuted.title: Upgrades from pre-17 clusters now fail where they used to succeed
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator upgrades a PG16 subscriber where one table is stuck in tablesync ('d' or 'f' state), or where an origin was dropped by hand. On HEAD this upgrade passes, because pre-17 subscription state is ignored. With v22, pg_upgrade refuses at the check stage, and the operator must fix sync on the old cluster first.
refuted.argument: Message #90 extends check_old_cluster_subscription_state() to every source version. The only reason is that tablesync origins (pg_<suboid>_<relid>) would otherwise be migrated and never dropped, which message #88 calls harmless. For pre-17 sources pg_subscription_rel is discarded anyway, so pg_dumpall could skip tablesync-named origins and the old cluster would not need to be blocked. Only Fujitsu reviewers agreed to this in messages #88-#90, and no committer has weighed the new rejection for released versions.
refuted.author_must_show: Why reject pre-17 sources with in-progress tablesync, when skipping tablesync origins from such sources would keep today's upgrade path working?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2, which covers both new refusals. Message #88 calls only the origin-less rejection harmless, and the material does not give the affiliation of every reviewer who agreed.

refuted.title: Main invariant only matters if pg_commit_ts migration is accepted
refuted.failure_scenario: The project adopts permanent pg_upgrade restrictions: the new cluster must hold no origins, and pre-17 sources get the new checks. If pg_commit_ts migration is never committed, preserved roidents protect no on-disk data. The project keeps the restrictions anyway and must defend them on their own.
refuted.argument: The v22 commit message presents the patch as a prerequisite for preserving pg_commit_ts. The patch's own documentation still says commit timestamps are not preserved. The thread does not say whether the pg_commit_ts patch from message #1 is accepted, so the roident invariant cannot be tested against real commit_ts data. Keeping user-created origins is a real gain on its own, but the thread argues the design mainly from the commit_ts case (messages #1, #26).
refuted.author_must_show: Is the pg_commit_ts migration patch agreed in principle, and would the restrictions in 0002 still be wanted if it never lands?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1. The restrictions it calls permanent are pg_upgrade checks and binary-upgrade support functions, which a later release can relax or remove.

refuted.title: Origin migration depends on naming conventions that future workers can break silently
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release adds a worker that creates its own origin named after the subscription OID. pg_dumpall copies that origin as an ordinary global object. Nothing in the new cluster links it to its subscription, so DROP SUBSCRIPTION leaves it behind, and users find the stale origins long after the upgrade.
refuted.argument: The 0001 commit message says origins link to subscriptions only by the names pg_<suboid> and pg_<suboid>_<relid>. The patch now copies every origin blindly, and correctness rests on a pre-check that rejects the known transient kinds. The tablesync case of this exact failure turned up only at v21 (message #88), after many review rounds. No test or assertion forces a future origin-creating feature to update check_old_cluster_subscription_state().
refuted.author_must_show: What makes a future origin-creating worker fail a test, instead of being migrated as an orphan origin, when its author forgets pg_upgrade?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a hypothetical future worker whose cleanup state is not migrated. The tablesync case arose only because sources before 17 do not migrate pg_subscription_rel; with subscription OIDs preserved, name-based links stay valid for newer sources.

refuted.title: Permanent roident invariant for a pg_commit_ts migration not yet accepted
refuted.failure_scenario: The project commits this patch, so every later pg_upgrade must preserve subscription OIDs and roident values. If the pg_commit_ts migration never lands, the project still keeps these support functions and a stricter new-cluster check, and its main stated motivation is gone.
refuted.argument: The 0002 commit message calls this "a prerequisite for preserving pg_commit_ts", and that migration lives in a separate thread whose status the material does not give. Message #26 says the exact roident "only matters from PG19" because of commit timestamps. The independent gain is that user-created origins survive the upgrade, but no message reports users or tools that lose origins today. The roident and OID guarantees are hard to take back once tools rely on them.
refuted.author_must_show: If the pg_commit_ts migration is not committed, which users need preserved roident values and origins from external tools, and what do they do today?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1. The claim that the guarantees are hard to take back is weak, because the binary-upgrade support functions are internal and are not a user-facing interface.

refuted.title: Upgrades from clusters before 17 now fail where they succeeded
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA upgrades a PG15 subscriber while one table is still in tablesync, or after an origin was dropped by hand. pg_upgrade now refuses during the checks. On HEAD the same upgrade succeeds and creates a fresh origin, so the DBA must first repair the old cluster.
refuted.argument: Message #90 extends check_old_cluster_subscription_state() to all old versions and removes the fallback that Nisha proposed in message #83. The thread calls the rejection harmless, but only Fujitsu reviewers agreed to it in messages #88 to #90. No committer has weighed this compatibility change. It exists only so that the patch does not migrate orphan tablesync origins, and skipping those origins at dump time would avoid it.
refuted.author_must_show: Why reject these old clusters rather than skip pg_<suboid>_<relid> origins at dump time when the source is before 17?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2. The statement that only Fujitsu reviewers agreed is not supported by the material for every reviewer.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: pg_upgrade now preserves pg_subscription.oid and roident, and adds new checks on old and new clusters.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: Replication origins and their remote_lsn are migrated, which changes where pre-17 subscriptions resume.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: pg_proc.dat gains two binary-upgrade support functions and loses binary_upgrade_replorigin_advance().

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes src/include/replication/origin.h and removes an existing support function.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dumpall --binary-upgrade emits all replication origins as global objects, and pg_dump emits the subscription OID.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Upgrades from released versions before 17 are now rejected in states that HEAD accepts.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Origin migration relies on the pg_<suboid> and pg_<suboid>_<relid> naming conventions and on pg_upgrade checks.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is the pg_commit_ts migration patch agreed for the same release, and if it does not land, which users need preserved roident values?
Why reject pre-17 clusters with relations not in 'i' or 'r' state instead of leaving pg_<suboid>_<relid> origins out of the dump for such sources?
Why reject a pre-17 subscription with a missing origin instead of creating a new origin for it, as HEAD does today?
For sources before 17, what stops an apply worker from creating a tablesync origin between check_old_cluster_subscription_state() and pg_dumpall?
Which external replication tools or users have reported that pg_upgrade loses their replication origins?

committability.owner_note: Amit Kapila steered the design in messages #26 and #51, but has not said the patch is ready. The owner needs to know logical replication origins and pg_upgrade of subscribers.
committability.liability: The owner signs for pg_upgrade of subscribers from every supported source version, including the new pre-17 refusals. The owner also signs for the roident guarantee that a later pg_commit_ts migration would depend on.
committability.author_follow_up: The authors posted 22 versions in about six months and kept the patch rebased across three CommitFests.

priority.reason: The patch helps subscribers that use pg_upgrade and need stable origin IDs, and users of external tools that create origins. It runs only in binary-upgrade mode, spans pg_dump, pg_upgrade and origin.c, and has an engaged committer and active authors.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check WAL logging of restored origin progress, locking in binary_upgrade_create_replication_origin(), or the binary-upgrade guard on the new functions. Only 3 of 90 messages were read directly.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Support for upgrading to checksums enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pg_upgrade run between clusters with different data checksum settings by rewriting page checksums while it copies files. The first version did this automatically in --copy mode, and a later version added an explicit --update-checksums option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author closed the entry because reviewers showed little interest in the feature or in solving its remaining problems. One problem was still open: copyFile() has a separate Windows code path, and the author did not know how checksum rewriting should work there. He said the feature could not move ahead without an answer to it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sensing much enthusiasm for this feature or for working out the
remaining problems, so I'm closing this commitfest entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade documentation improvement
precedents_retrieved.summary: A documentation patch for pg_upgrade explained what "compatible initdb flags" means for the new cluster: the same encoding, locale and checksum settings as the old one. It told users to find the encoding and locale of template0 with psql -l and the checksum setting with pg_controldata.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut said the cluster locale is better taken from pg_controldata and doubted that pg_upgrade needs the encoding to match. The author asked whether to change the patch to use pg_controldata only, but no revised patch followed. Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback because the thread had died.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
A better way to get the
*cluster* locale is from pg_controldata.

precedents_retrieved.title: add timing information to pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the elapsed time of each pg_upgrade step to the status output, for example "ok (took 82 ms)", formatted like psql's PrintTiming(). The goal was to show where upgrade time goes and to measure future work on reducing pg_upgrade downtime.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut questioned who besides developers would use the timings and said pg_upgrade output already has too much information that users cannot act on. He suggested that shell tools such as "pg_upgrade | ts" or "ts -i" are enough, and the author agreed to leave it at that unless someone saw a reason to build it in. Only a related fix that raised MESSAGE_WIDTH to 62 was committed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If it's just for developers and expert users, perhaps existing
shell-level functionality like "pg_upgrade | ts" would suffice?

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow using replication origins in SQL level parallel sessions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a variant pg_replication_origin_session_setup(text, int) so that several SQL sessions can use the same replication origin at once. Logical replication parallel apply workers already share an origin this way, and the patch exposes that to external replication systems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila pointed out that another thread already discusses the same feature and asked the author to give input there. The entry was then withdrawn, so the work appears to have continued in that other thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We are already discussing the same feature in an email thread [1]. Can
you check that and share your inputs there?

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade version and path checking
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set makes pg_upgrade check every executable it uses, require the new binaries to match pg_upgrade's exact major and minor version, and default --new-bindir to pg_upgrade's own directory. It came from Tom Lane's report that pg_upgrade 11.3 would use pg_dump 11.1.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed 0002 to 0004, which add the executable checks, the --new-bindir default and a typo fix. He found that 0001 compares pg_upgrade's version only with pg_ctl's, so it does not make all binaries match, and proposed a version check for each validate_exec() call instead. On 2019-09-02 the author said a new version would come that week, but no later version appears in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It compares (new_cluster.bin_version != PG_VERSION_NUM), but new_cluster.bin_version is actually just the version of pg_ctl, so this is just comparing the version of pg_upgrade with the version of pg_ctl, which is not wrong, but doesn't really achieve the full goal of having all binaries match.

precedents_retrieved.title: Preserve versions of initdb-created collations in pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make pg_upgrade preserve the recorded versions of collations created by initdb. In binary-upgrade mode, pg_dump would delete all initdb-created collations in the new cluster and dump CREATE COLLATION commands with version information, instead of updating the existing objects in place.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review showed that the patch makes the pg_upgrade check fail for clusters initialized with SQL_ASCII encoding, where ICU collations for that encoding do not exist, and that it leaves the recreated collations looking like user-defined objects. The author then questioned the approach and suggested not creating collations in initdb at all. The reviewer replied that the problem would go away if the separate per-object collation version patch set were committed, since that drops the collversion column. The author then marked the patch Returned with Feedback without further changes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this problem goes away if we commit the per-object collation
version patch set[1].

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Pass -j option down to vacuumdb
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Michael Paquier, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_upgrade pass its -j option to the vacuumdb commands in the generated analyze_new_cluster.sh script, so the post-upgrade analyze runs in parallel. Later versions added a VACUUM_OPTS variable to the script and a suggested vacuumdb --jobs command.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers held that pg_upgrade -j and vacuumdb -j are bound by different resources, so the same value should not be reused, and the generated script is meant to analyze gently. Tom Lane and Michael Paquier did not see most of the patch as better than the status quo and preferred a printed hint or a documentation-only change. The thread then moved to copying statistics in pg_upgrade instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So based on that linking the value used by pg_upgrade and vacuumdb is a bad concept in my opinion, and the patch should be rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve documentation for pg_upgrade, standbys and rsync
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch rewrites the pg_upgrade documentation for upgrading standbys with rsync: it recommends rsync --relative, updates the version numbers and paths in the examples, and adds a reminder to create standby.signal. Later versions also add SQL steps to drop leftover temporary tables and truncate unlogged tables before the rsync, and reorder the preparation steps.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Stephen Frost argued that this procedure is too hard to get right in an rsync command or a documented procedure, and that a tool should replace it. He proposed moving the text out of the documentation to a wiki. Robert Haas found the new order of the preparation steps confusing. The author saw no agreement and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
To be more explicit though- we should write a tool to do this.  We
shouldn't try to document a way to do it because it's hard to get right.

roaster_notes.note: The thread also reports, in message #2, an earlier attempt to preserve subscription OIDs that stalled for lack of motivation; it is not in the precedent list. [P19] concerns a buildfarm-flaky test for relfilenode preservation, and its reason does not apply here.

Other contract changes were settled in the thread. The empty-new-cluster rule was discussed in message #26, the resume position in message #86, and the max_active_replication_origins check in messages #51-#71.
Objections found; see list. Not checked without code: WAL logging of restored origin progress, and catalog locking in the new support function.

The proposal has no real privilege or exposure aspect. The new binary_upgrade_* functions run only in binary-upgrade mode, pg_dumpall output already requires superuser, and replication origins are superuser-managed objects today. The quoting of origin names in the dump was raised in message #9 and fixed in message #10. Whether the new support functions keep the usual binary-upgrade guard cannot be checked without the code.

No hot-path cost was found: all changes run in pg_upgrade or binary-upgrade mode. Amit Kapila, a committer in this area, engaged in the design (messages #26 and #51), which lowers the item 16 concern.

Postgres has no existing way to choose a roident or a subscription OID, and pg_replication_origin_create() always takes the lowest free ID, so this cannot be done outside pg_upgrade today. Recreating user origins by hand after the upgrade restores names and remote_lsn but not their IDs, and no extension or hook covers binary-upgrade restore.
Only one demand concern: the value depends on a separate pg_commit_ts patch. The case for user-created origins has no field reports, but it is a plausible correctness gain at low cost.
